problem_markdown: Can one select 1983 distinct integers from $1,\ldots,100000$ with no three forming an arithmetic progression? Prove the answer.
solutions_markdown:
Yes. Consider all integers with at most eleven ternary digits, each digit zero or one. There are $2^{11}=2048$ such integers, ranging from zero to $(3^{11}-1)/2=88573$.

If three members satisfy $x+z=2y$, neither the addition on the left nor the doubling on the right involves carries in base three. Digitwise, $x_i+z_i=2y_i$ with all digits in $\{0,1\}$. If $y_i=0$, both other digits are zero; if $y_i=1$, both are one. Thus $x=y=z$, so no nonconstant three-term progression occurs.

Add one to every member. This preserves the absence of progressions and produces 2048 positive integers at most 88574. Any 1983 of them are a valid selection.
